claim: Vitest 4 (October 2025) removed the experimental tag from Browser Mode and shipped codemods that automate the Jest-to-Vitest migration.
quote: Stable Browser Mode: The experimental tag has been removed, making browser-based testing production-ready

claim: Vitest Browser Mode is configured with a provider factory (playwright/webdriverio/preview) and an instances array; the docs carry no experimental banner.
quote: import { playwright } from '@vitest/browser-playwright' ... test: { browser: { provider: playwright(), enabled: true, instances: [{ browser: 'chromium' }] } }

claim: Next.js officially states Vitest cannot render async Server Components and recommends E2E tests for them.
quote: Since `async` Server Components are new to the React ecosystem, Vitest currently does not support them. While you can still run unit tests for synchronous Server and Client Components, we recommend using E2E tests for `async` components.

claim: react-hook-form's act warnings come from its always-async validation resolving after the test function returns; the fix is awaiting find*/waitFor, not wrapping render in act().
quote: the validation in react-hook-form is always async, so you have to wait until it is finished ... wait until some element from your UI appears with find* queries ... you must not wrap your render() calls in act()

claim: Schema unit tests should assert safeParse success/failure plus the exact error path and message, and focus on custom .refine/.superRefine/.transform logic.
quote: Thoroughly test your `.refine()`, `.superRefine()`, and `.transform()` methods to ensure your custom validation and transformation logic works as expected.

claim: zod-fast-check derives fast-check arbitraries from a Zod schema for property-based testing of parse/transform round-trips.
quote: Generate fast-check arbitraries from Zod schemas.

claim: fast-check is the mainstream TypeScript property-based testing library.
quote: Property based testing framework for JavaScript/TypeScript

claim: Vitest exposes vi.advanceTimersByTime and the async variant vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync for driving debounce timers deterministically.
quote: vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000) fast-forwards the timer

claim: Testing Library documents that combining fake timers with user-event causes timeouts unless the advanceTimers option is passed to userEvent.setup().
quote: Combining fake timers with `user-event` may cause test timeouts. Refer to `advanceTimers` option to prevent this issue.

claim: userEvent.click() hangs/fails under vi.useFakeTimers() when advanceTimers is not wired up — a long-standing open issue.
quote: `userEvent.click()` fails when used with `vi.useFakeTimers()`, all available solutions are not working

claim: For debounced async work you must use advanceTimersByTimeAsync, which flushes microtasks between timer callbacks, otherwise the promise/timer chain deadlocks.
quote: use `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` instead of `advanceTimersByTime`, as the async variant flushes microtasks between timer executions

claim: userEvent.type() with react-hook-form mode:'onChange' produces act() warnings because the onChange validation resolves after type() returns.
quote: The onChange event from the input happens asynchronously so userEvent.type ends before it gets called.

claim: user-event already wraps interactions in act(); wrapping them again yields the contradictory 'testing environment is not configured to support act' warning.
quote: Test warns that I need to use `act` for user actions, then warns act is not configured if I do

claim: Clicking a real submit button in jsdom logs 'Not implemented: HTMLFormElement.prototype.requestSubmit' — the most common form-testing false alarm.
quote: Submitting a form by clicking on submit button throws jsdom console errors for unimplemented submit

claim: jsdom deliberately does not implement navigation, which includes native form submission.
quote: Error: Not implemented: HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit

claim: Vitest's official component-testing guide uses vitest-browser-react's render plus the page.getByRole locator API and its own userEvent, not @testing-library/user-event.
quote: Use `vitest/browser` for user interactions instead of `@testing-library/user-event`

claim: vitest-browser-react is the official React renderer for Vitest Browser Mode.
quote: Render React components in Vitest Browser Mode

claim: Vitest Browser Mode runs roughly 2-3x slower than jsdom, while Playwright's component testing remains experimental in 2026.
quote: Vitest browser mode performance: surprisingly fast — tests run in headless Chromium, parallel across workers, ~2-3x slower than JSDOM

claim: Browser Mode fixes jsdom gaps (missing IntersectionObserver, fake getBoundingClientRect, unreliable focus/hover/pointer) and needs headless + low maxWorkers on CI.
quote: Browser Mode reached stable status in Vitest 4.0, so it is no longer experimental.

claim: Vitest documents that simulated environments diverge from real browsers and that spinning up a browser costs initialization time.
quote: only simulate a browser environment and not an actual browser, which may result in some discrepancies between the simulated environment and the real environment

claim: useActionState takes an action of shape (previousState, formData) => newState and returns [state, dispatchAction, isPending]; passing dispatchAction to <form action> wraps submission in a Transition.
quote: When used this way, React automatically wraps the submission in a Transition, so you don't need to call startTransition yourself.

claim: The community pattern for unit-testing Server Actions is to import the exported async function, call it with a hand-built FormData, and vi.mock the Next.js internals (redirect, revalidatePath, next/headers).
quote: vi.mock("next/navigation", () => ({ redirect: (path: string) => path }));

claim: There is still no official Next.js guidance for testing useActionState/useFormStatus components with React Testing Library; the discussion remains unanswered by maintainers.
quote: I unit tested forms and server actions using several mocks and React 18.3(canary). With React 18.2 I wasn't able to make it.

claim: MSW's maintainer rejects mocking RSC/Server-Action payloads in the browser as 'extremely dangerous' framework-internal mocking and points to setupRemoteServer for server-side interception.
quote: If you are mocking an RSC response, you are no longer drawing a boundary at the network request your app makes. Now, you are mocking the internals of your framework to make it return different components. That's extremely dangerous and can break your app.

claim: MSW intercepts requests at the network level, so components exercise their real fetch/axios code paths.
quote: Mock Service Worker intercepts requests on the network level

claim: MSW is the wrong seam for anything that does not cross the HTTP boundary — feature flags, localStorage, clocks, layout measurements.
quote: MSW is a poor fit for behavior that does not cross the HTTP boundary. Do not use it to fake local storage, feature flag hooks, date functions, browser permissions, or layout measurements.

claim: Playwright's official guidance: test user-visible behavior, prefer role-based locators, use auto-retrying web-first assertions, and mock third-party network rather than driving external sites.
quote: By using web first assertions Playwright will wait until the expected condition is met

claim: Playwright uploads files with locator.setInputFiles(), supports in-memory buffers, and handles custom pickers via the filechooser event.
quote: await page.getByLabel('Upload file').setInputFiles({ name: 'file.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('this is test') });

claim: Playwright is the default E2E runner in 2026.
quote: Playwright is a framework for Web Testing and Automation.

claim: Vitest is the Vite-native test runner and the default recommendation for new React/TS projects in 2026.
quote: Next generation testing framework powered by Vite.

claim: Playwright still cannot drive the browser's native autofill UI; the feature request is open and labelled P3-collecting-feedback.
quote: [Feature] Testing Autofill behavior ... Chrome Devtools Protocol has added support for autofill interaction, and Puppeteer has added support for this feature.

claim: Jest 30 still wins for CommonJS codebases, 10k+ test suites needing battle-tested --shard, and Angular/React Native ecosystems.
quote: Jest's `--shard` implementation is more mature; Vitest added sharding in v1 but Jest's is more battle-tested for 10K+ test suites
